title: Linear & Ridge Regression with Gradient Descent
summary: Derive MSE gradients, add an L2 penalty and make batch gradient descent converge to the least-squares solution.

ShapeMismatch.hint: Your arrays are broadcasting unexpectedly. Print X.shape, w.shape and y.shape inside each function; a (m,) minus (m, 1) silently becomes (m, m).

NotConverging.hint: Descent is diverging or stalling. Check the sign of the update (w - lr * dw) and that the gradient is divided by m.

hints.test_predict_shape: ŷ = X @ w + b should have one entry per row of X.
hints.test_gradient_shapes_and_types: dw needs one entry per feature (shape (n,)); db is a single scalar. Xᵀ @ residual gives you the right shape.
hints.test_cost_known_value: Use 1/(2m) in front of the sum of squared residuals, and return a plain Python float.
hints.test_cost_with_l2_penalty: The penalty is (λ / 2m)·‖w‖². It uses the same 2m denominator as the data term.
hints.test_gradients_match_finite_differences: Differentiate J term by term. The data term gives (1/m)·Xᵀ(ŷ − y) and the penalty gives (λ/m)·w.
hints.test_bias_is_not_regularized: λ should only appear in the weight gradient. The bias gradient is just the mean residual.
hints.test_converges_to_closed_form: If the weights are close but not exact, check that w and b are updated simultaneously from gradients computed at the same point.
hints.test_cost_history_length_and_monotonic: Record the cost after every update (exactly n_iters entries). A rising cost usually means a flipped sign.
hints.test_ridge_shrinks_weights: Make sure lam is actually forwarded from gradient_descent to compute_gradients.
hints.test_inputs_not_mutated: Avoid in-place operators like X -= ... or y /= ... on the arguments you receive.
hints.test_no_forbidden_solvers: The goal is to reach the solution iteratively, so closed-form solvers are off-limits.
